subject: Discovery recap — Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Chris Patel <chris.patel@aurorafinance.com>, Aurora Finance Platform Team <platform@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Hi Chris / Platform team,

Thanks again for taking time earlier today — appreciate the context. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can move to a sizing/proposal: 

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes during end-of-day settlements causing customer-facing timeouts (~99th percentile spikes to 1.2s).
- Cost volatility on burst traffic when using shared on-demand GPUs.
- Need for stronger isolation/compliance for sensitive PII workloads (auditability + KMS).

Current stack as described:
- Inference: in-house endpoints on GKE backed by mixed GPU fleet (shared).
- Autoscaling: k8s HPA based on CPU + custom queue length for model workers.
- Models: mix of open LLMs and a tuned LLM family (mostly 7B–13B variants).

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Predictable baseline throughput: ~500 req/s sustained (avg), with 10-min bursts up to ~1,500 req/s.
- p99 latency target < 250ms for request types marked "low-latency".
- Encryption at rest + in transit, KMS for keys, and audit logs for inference requests.
- Clear unit economics (goal: reduce per-token variability and total TCO).

What we recommend next (high level):
1) Redwood Dedicated reserved pool sized for your baseline throughput (we typically model baseline + headroom).
2) Burst autoscaling policy for short windows (we can support short-duration burst capacity and controlled spillover to hosted fallback).
3) Private VPC attachment + KMS integration for isolation and auditability.
4) Technical deep-dive with infra + SRE to finalize sizing assumptions (seq length, model family, concurrency).

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Capacity_Overview.pdf (high-level), Sizing_Template.xlsx (we'll use this to collect metrics needed for final sizing).

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You: share a quick export of 1 week of traffic (req/s distribution by minute, median/99 latency by endpoint, avg seq length) using the attached sizing template — if you prefer, send an anonymized sample.
- We: schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (proposal: Tue 15 Jun, 10am PT) and draft a preliminary capacity proposal & ballpark pricing within 3 business days after the deep-dive.

Let me know whether Tue 15th 10am PT works; if not, share two alternatives and we’ll lock something in.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | (415) 555-0179

--
Redwood Inference — High-performance inference for production LLMs
From: Chris Patel <chris.patel@aurorafinance.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Finance Platform Team <platform@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Thanks Rafael — great recap, this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Burst behavior: the 1,500 req/s bursts are real but typically only last ~5–15 minutes at end-of-day. Important that the service doesn't degrade for other tenants (isolation).
- Models: primary inference workload is a tuned 13B model (seq len ~512 average, occasional 2k requests). We also run smaller 7B models for lower-priority tasks.
- Data retention: logs for inference calls need to be retained for 90 days for audit, and we need redaction options for PII.
- Compliance: SOC2 in-scope; we'll need to review your SOC2 report and encryption/HSM support.

We can get you an anonymized traffic export by EOD Mon 15 Jun. The Tue 15th 10am PT time works for a tech deep-dive — I’ll accept the invite if you send it.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity priced as on-demand minutes (i.e., an additional hourly rate for burst) and whether you offer a cross-region fallback for DR?

Thanks,
Chris
Chris Patel
VP Platform Engineering | Aurora Finance
chris.patel@aurorafinance.com

Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap — Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Raf — forwarding my quick notes / suggested approach before we draft the proposal.

Key recommendations:
- Baseline capacity: size reserved pool to cover 600 req/s sustained (adds 20% headroom to your baseline ask of 500) to avoid tight headroom.
- Burst plan: enable short-window autoscaling up to 1,800 req/s with a max burst window of 15 minutes; price bursts as "burst-minutes" with capped hourly rate — keeps predictability.
- Isolation: recommend Private VPC + customer-managed KMS; include optional HSM integration for keys if they need FIPS/HSM.
- Reliability: plan for a cross-region fallback (warm standby in a second region) — useful for DR but can be optional in initial contract.

Attachments: SOW_template_v2.docx (use this for statement-of-work skeleton).

Ask: once you get the traffic export from Chris, we should run our sizing model (I can help) and produce a 1-page TCO comparison (current vs Redwood Dedicated).

-Marissa

1) Calendar invite: I’ve scheduled a 60-min technical deep-dive for Tue, 15 Jun 2026, 10:00–11:00 AM PT — link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=aurora-tech-deep-dive-20260615 (please accept).
2) Data we need from your side (populate the attached Sizing_Template.xlsx if possible):
   - Minute-level req/s distribution for the last 7 days
   - Median and p99 latency by endpoint
   - Average and 95th seq length distribution
   - Primary model family (you said tuned 13B) and any quantization/FP requirements
3) Compliance artifacts: I’ll email our SOC2 summary and an outline of KMS/HSM options prior to the meeting.
4) Proposal: we’ll deliver a preliminary Redwood Dedicated proposal (capacity sizing + ballpark pricing + SOW) within 3 business days after the deep-dive. I attached a draft we can iterate on: Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_Draft.pdf.

If you want, we can also run a short canary (1–2 days) on a fraction of traffic to validate latency under your workload before committing to full reserved capacity.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
